title: Barnette's conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's proof (2026) of Barnette's conjecture: every cubic, bipartite, 3-connected graph carrying a sphere map (in particular every such planar graph) has a Hamiltonian cycle, and one avoiding any prescribed edge. The first lesson develops sphere maps (rotation systems with Euler characteristic 2) combinatorially: deletion, duality, trees and cotrees, the two sides of a cycle, an Euler count for a side, and the faces of a connected submap. The second shows that the dual of such a graph is a face-coloured sphere triangulation and cuts along separating triangles. The third proves that two disjoint face-vertex matchings (a pair of states) exist by an integral flow and a density inequality. The fourth proves a disk identity and evaluates a finite exponential sum over pairs in two ways, with positive circulations on spokes, to find a pair whose opposite edges form a forest. The fifth turns that pair into two induced trees, glues across separating triangles, and reads off the Hamiltonian cycle.

open_obligations: Embedding theorem (Theorem 5.1 of the first lesson): the rotation system of a plane embedding of a connected finite graph is a sphere map whose faces are the boundary walks of the regions. Classical, based on the Jordan curve theorem; not proved in the programme. Used only for Corollary 6.2 of the fifth lesson (the planar form); Theorem 6.1, stated for graphs carrying a sphere map, is proved in full. Intended home: a lesson on plane embeddings and rotation systems.

Pfaffian consequence (Remark (b) in Section 6 of the fifth lesson): every path with three edges in a cubic 3-connected bipartite Pfaffian graph lies in a Hamiltonian cycle. It follows from Theorem 6.1 through the equivalence of Gorsky, Steiner and Wiederrecht (Theorem 4.16 of arXiv:2202.11641, as cited by OpenAI), which is not proved in the programme.
